## The permutation null distribution

```{r}
#| label: null-distribution
#| results: asis
#| fig-height: 3.4
if (is.null(null_df) || nrow(null_df) == 0 || !any(null_df$kind == "null")) {
  cat(paste("\nThis correction does not produce a cluster-mass distribution, so there is",
            "nothing to draw here. TFCE scores every point by the support it gathers across",
            "thresholds rather than forming discrete clusters to sum over.\n\n"))
} else {
  nulls <- null_df %>% filter(kind == "null")
  obs   <- null_df %>% filter(kind == "observed")

  # One panel per tail. A two-tailed test has two distributions and two
  # sets of observed clusters, and overlaying them would put a negative
  # cluster mass on the positive null it was never compared against.
  p <- ggplot(nulls, aes(x = value)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey70", colour = NA) +
    facet_wrap(~ tail, scales = "free") +
    labs(x = "cluster mass under relabelling", y = "permutations") +
    alz_theme()
  if (nrow(obs) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(data = obs, aes(xintercept = value),
                        colour = "#c1272d", linewidth = 0.7)
  }
  print(p)
  cat("\n\n")

  # The proportion of the null at least as extreme as the largest
  # observed cluster, stated per tail. This is the Monte-Carlo p-value
  # from its own definition, so a reader can check the number in the
  # table above against the picture rather than trusting the label.
  for (tl in unique(nulls$tail)) {
    nd <- nulls$value[nulls$tail == tl]
    od <- obs$value[obs$tail == tl]
    if (length(od) == 0) next
    extreme <- if (identical(tl, "positive")) max(od) else min(od)
    share <- if (identical(tl, "positive")) mean(nd >= extreme) else mean(nd <= extreme)
    cat(sprintf("On the %s tail, %s of %d relabellings produced a cluster at least as extreme as the largest observed one (mass %s).\n\n",
                tl, format(round(share * length(nd))), length(nd), apa_num(extreme)))
  }
}
```
